tasks.title: Concurrent cell prepares keep invalidating each other's readiness validation
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (design choice). Seen 2026-10-31 on Portswood Rec (53,-42) with neighbour sessions preparing 52,-42/52,-43: `prepare --apply` on one cell changed the readiness revision of neighbouring cells, so a separate prepare then apply was refused 'validation stale' four times; builders had to chain prepare && apply in one shell command. Revision = content_id([POLICY, facts revision, plan_identity]) in lib/journal/cell_readiness.py; I did not find which input changes (suspect vector-map extract rewrite or neighbour plan notes). Questions: should validation of cell A depend on neighbour state at all? Should apply refresh validation itself under the lock? Decide, then fix.

tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. I dismissed both with dismiss-feature. Decide whether prepare should skip groups already covered by a spec-backed plan, and how legacy bare ids should be matched.

tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (policy). Decide: warn/confirm before an apply touches a done neighbour; keep or drop frontier ghost generation on feature applies; whether edge fringe (roof overhang) should invalidate trees/decor at all.

tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Decor, trees and ground dry runs on a built cell understate the plan and overwrite tracked reports
tasks.notes:
Found in #244 (2026-11-16). `python3 scripts/decor_layer.py --world W --cell C` (dry run) on a cell that is already built treats the cell's own decor mask as blocked, so it understates the plan: #244 reported 305 blocks on 53,-43 instead of about 2,716 and every front hedge failed as 'blocked by live or owned block' (numbers from #244, not re-measured; the last real apply, world commit 8447beb on 2026-11-14, placed 2,695). A real rebuild undoes first, so only the dry run misleads. The dry run also overwrote tracked world files (the 53,-43 decor report and preview).

Files: lib/layers/decor_layer.py (plan_cell loads masks ~625; dry run `run` ~806; `apply_cell` ~844), lib/layers/trees_layer.py (`run` ~731-772), lib/layers/ground_layer.py (dry run ~1277-1319), lib/layers/layer_reports.py (`write_report`), lib/site/site_kit.py (`Plan.bounds` ~238, `preview` ~345), scripts/trees_replan.py (`replan`, the precedent), tests lib/layers/test_decor_layer.py, test_trees_layer.py, test_ground_layer.py, test_layer_reports.py, scripts/test_trees_replan.py.

Causes (read from the code on main, 2026-11-19):
- Understating: the own mask's positions are in the `masked` set AND the live world still holds the old blocks, so both the mask test and the `is_air` test refuse the cell's own columns. Subtracting the mask alone is not enough.
- Overwriting: `write_report(name, ...)` writes `verification/site/<name>-report.json` in the dry run and again in `apply_cell`, so a dry run replaces the last apply's report. The preview, crowns, plan and kinds files are written only by dry runs, into the same tracked folder.
- Trees crash: `Plan.bounds()` does `zip(*self.cells)` and raises on an empty plan; `trees_layer.run` calls `preview` and `apply(dry=True)` unconditionally, where decor guards with `if placed:`.
- Note: layer_redo.py is NOT the precedent: it shells out to `mask_undo.py --apply` (a real undo). The precedent is scripts/trees_replan.py `replan()`: `plan_undo` for the cleared positions, `PlannedWorld(Plan, world, ignore=cleared)` so old blocks read as air, and `TreeInputs.after_undo(remaining_masks)`.

Change:
1. Decor dry run plans as if the cell's own decor mask were undone, as trees_replan does for trees. Factor the shared part of `trees_replan.replan` (own-mask cleared positions via `pass_mask.plan_undo`, a `PlannedWorld` whose ignore set is those positions, masked set = every other mask) into one helper that trees_replan and the decor dry run both use; do not write a second copy. If `plan_undo` reports conflicts, the dry run says so and plans against the unmodified world (it must not raise). Real apply and redo keep their present behaviour.
2. Trees dry run uses the same helper, so it too plans as if its own trees mask were undone (today it does not, which is why trees_replan.py exists). Ground dry run: no change to planning; it reports mask conflicts on purpose ('NOT SAFE TO APPLY: undo the listed mask first') and hiding them would be wrong. Say in the commit message that ground was checked.
3. A dry run writes only `-dry` names: `<name>-dry-report.json`, `<name>-dry-preview.png` (trees also `<name>-dry-crowns.png`, `<name>-dry-plan.json`; ground `<name>-dry-kinds.png`, `<name>-dry-preview.png`). Add a `dry` flag to `write_report` and build every artifact path through one helper so tests can redirect it (several paths are hard-coded from ROOT today). Apply keeps the present names. A dry run never writes an apply-named file.
4. Empty plan in the trees dry run: do not call `preview` or `apply(dry=True)` when nothing is placed; print that no preview was written (as decor does).
Out of scope: restoring the tracked 53,-43 files the earlier dry runs overwrote (a checkout of world commit 8447beb's versions; the owner's call); the world's .gitignore. Not a stretch by the model-and-effort rules only if the shared helper stays small; if it grows into a rewrite of trees_replan, stop and report.

Tests: (a) decor: a fake world holding the old own-mask blocks plus a recorded mask gives a dry-run placement count equal to a planning run on an empty world, and no row refused 'blocked by live or owned block' for the cell's own columns; same for trees; (b) a dry run leaves an existing `<name>-report.json` and `<name>-preview.png` byte-identical and creates the `-dry` names, for decor, trees and ground; (c) a real apply still writes the unsuffixed names; (d) the trees dry run on an empty plan does not raise. Update the two existing tests that mock `layer_reports.write_report` with `lambda n, r:` (test_decor_layer.py ~650 and test_ground_layer.py ~1006) for the new `dry` argument, and the decor test that asserts the file name `highfield_0_0_decor-report.json` (it becomes `-dry-`).
Check: `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_decor_layer` (and test_trees_layer, test_ground_layer, test_layer_reports, test_trees_replan) pass. Orchestrator after merge (needs the world data and an MCP flush): the decor dry run on 53,-43 reports close to the last apply (2,695), not a few hundred, and `git -C worlds/southampton-build status` shows no tracked verification file changed.

tasks.title: Pitched roof ridges: a one-wide ridge top is a bottom-half slab, a two-wide ridge top is a pair of stairs facing each other
tasks.notes:
Issue: Roof ridge tops are full blocks, not slabs or opposed stairs (I-047), owner snag S-083 (West). Moved off I-019, which no fix covers.

Before starting: check that no task merged since 2026-11-17 has already given ridge tops a cap rule (checked 2026-11-17: #125, #149, #207, #209, #300, #302 only handle odd half-steps and slab tops beside stairs, none handles ridges; a synthetic run on main confirms full blocks at the top). Re-run the two profiles below on current main; if they already give a slab or stair pair, close this as already done.

Cause: pitched_roof_states (lib/builds/feature_build.py ~823) gives a stair only to a cell with a neighbour at least 2 half-steps higher. A ridge cell has none, so an even-height ridge gets a full block whether 1 or 2 wide; a 2-wide odd ridge gets two slabs between full-block flanks. Profiles across x: [0,2,4,6,4,2,0] gives a full block at the top; [0,2,4,6,6,4,2,0] gives two full blocks. Not verified: how many ridge cells on real West (west_w34391673), David Kiddle (w146985470) and Hartley (w33830050) plans are 1 or 2 wide; the in-game look.

Change: in pitched_roof_states, after regularising, find ridge runs: an N4-connected set of equal-height cells with no higher N4 neighbour, bounding box 1xN or 2xN, narrow axis bounded both sides by lower roof cells (a zone-level boundary is not a lower roof cell). Width 1: bottom-half slab at roof_block_y(h) with a solid block below (reuse the wall-under-slab path). Width 2: two stairs at roof_block_y(h), each facing the other (facing here is the upslope direction, so both high backs meet in the middle and the peak is kept). Odd 2-wide ridges: two opposed stairs too. A cell that already gets a stair in the first pass (a higher neighbour, or a diagonal rise) is never a ridge cell. A hip apex (1x1) takes a slab. 2x2 blocks, L/T shapes, wider decks and runs with a higher neighbour at the end stay as they are.
Trade-off the owner accepted: a slab ridge sits half a block lower than today's full-block ridge (lidar is a guide for roofs); the stair pair keeps today's height for an even half-height h; for an odd h the stair at roof_block_y(h) peaks half a block higher than today's two slabs (accepted; do not drop to h-1; assumption to confirm with the owner when reviewing West).
Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py (pitched_roof_states, and its second caller roof_pitched ~2465-2505, the Chebyshev hip, which changes too), rules/feature-builds.md (roof text ~177-188), lib/builds/test_feature_build.py (update test_gable_stairs_face_upslope_ridge_full, which asserts a full block at a one-wide ridge; check test_pitched_zones_ridge_slabs_flat_plateaus_unchanged). Tests: 1-wide and 2-wide, even and odd; 3-wide deck stays full; run ends; hip apex; zone boundary; same-Y stair shape rule; slab support block. Also a test through roof_pitched (1x1 apex and 2-wide ridge on a rectangular hip footprint). roof_lint (lib/audit/roof_lint.py _ridges accepts a 0-cell cap and a 1-cell cap): ridge jogs and stair-shape mismatches are clean on synthetic plans built with the new rule (a test); on the real plans only after the rebuild (orchestrator).
Check: after rebuilding West, python3 scripts/roof_lint.py reports no ridge jogs and no stair-shape mismatches; in game its one-wide ridges are bottom-half slabs, two-wide ridges are stair pairs meeting at a peak, wide decks stay full blocks.
On landing: the orchestrator logs the fix on I-047 with a check line for S-083 (issues.py fix); the implementer does not write to the world registry.


Do not: run builds, undo, redo or any live-world command; take the site lock; change anything under worlds/; widen this task to terrace edges or to flat roof areas built with stairs. Out of scope, owner decision 2026-11-19: terrace edges (a full block with no higher neighbour that is not a ridge; I-019 S-086, which names this task but is not covered by it) have no task yet; flat areas built with stairs are I-048 (open, not diagnosed).
Decided, do not reopen: a 1-wide ridge and a 1x1 hip apex are a bottom-half slab; a 2-wide ridge is an opposed stair pair; 3-wide and wider decks stay full blocks.
Evidence for the commit message: factor the ridge detection into a pure helper that takes half_heights (and levels) and returns runs with their width. Count ridge runs of width 1, 2 and other on West (west_w34391673), David Kiddle (w146985470) and Hartley (w33830050) by recovering half-heights from their recorded roof cells (full block or stair at y is 2y, a bottom-half slab at y is 2y-1; an approximation, say so), read-only through the journal (scripts/roof_lint.py shows how it reads recorded plans). No builder dry run: that needs the live world.
Shipping: the orchestrator ships it through ship-branch (independent review); a wrong roof shape only shows at the next rebuild.

tasks.title: Decor places picnic tables: footprint recipe, map tag, designer kind
tasks.notes:
First step: read the design note from #305 and amend this task's Change where the note differs; the note wins. Then build.

Design note (from #305, decided; the note wins over the text below): docs/specs/decor-furniture-footprints.md. Amendments to the Change: (a) two kinds, picnic_table (map point and designer, rectangular, 9 voxels) and picnic_table_round (designer only, a plus of 5 voxels), recipes in a new FOOTPRINTS table of (dx, dz, dy, block) anchored at the centre column, rotation 0/90/180/270 clockwise, FURNITURE_KINDS replaces the `in sf.RECIPES` tests; (b) a map point is always rotation 0 (the Hampshire extract's 30 Highfield picnic tables carry no `direction` tag); (c) place_furniture takes keep_clear and barrier_voxels, applies reserved_gap per footprint column (plan_cell no longer pre-splits on the anchor), and returns the new reasons `crosses the cell edge`, `uneven ground`, `overlaps a planned barrier`, `overlaps another furniture item`; (d) bench slabs must be added to plan.keep_slab_cells or rewrite_bottom_half_slabs turns them into full blocks; (e) report rows carry rotation and footprint, refused rows blocked_column; (f) the test list is section 12 of the note. Merge order: #303 (in flight on task/303-layer-dry-runs) edits plan_cell and run in lib/layers/decor_layer.py; branch #306 from main after #303 merges, or rebase onto it.

Issue: Decor places no street furniture (I-008), owner snag S-033 (picnic tables on the plaza and round picnic tables on the north-west lawn of 48,-44 are missing). Blocked by the footprint design spike.

Cause: furniture is single-column (one top per item, recipes of (dy, block)), so a table with a bench each side cannot be expressed; lib/sources/street_furniture.py KINDS has no picnic_table (bench, waste_basket, bicycle_parking, street_lamp, bollard, sign). The map extract cannot find leisure=picnic_table: the osmconf points layer (config/osmconf.ini line 8, with copies at worlds/*/downloads/osmconf.ini per #182) lists name, barrier, highway, amenity, natural, entrance, traffic_sign, information, man_made, with no leisure, and classify() has no leisure branch. The 2026-10-27 designer reading of 48,-44 (reference/decor-furniture.json) listed 22 bicycle_parking and 3 bench items and left NW-garden tables out as 'not placeable' (registry/decisions/highfield_48_m44_decor.json) before the lawn rule allowed lawn. 'picnic' appears nowhere in lib, scripts or rules. Not verified: how many tables the aerial shows.
Change: kind 'picnic_table' with a footprint recipe (per the spike), every footprint column checked by the existing filters (lawn, gravel and paving allowed; carriageway, door routes and openings refused) or the whole table refused with a reason. Add an other_tags match for leisure=picnic_table in EXTRACT_JOBS (the points layer has other_tags=yes and classify already receives other_tags merged) plus a classify branch; adding leisure to the osmconf attributes is optional. Existing worlds need a re-extract (world work; the worlds/*/downloads copies of osmconf.ini are not tracked). Designer items accept the kind (anchor, rotation); the report carries provenance. Tests in lib/sources/test_street_furniture.py, lib/layers/test_decor_layer.py and lib/layers/test_decor_plan.py: placed on lawn, refused on a carriageway, refused when one footprint column is blocked, designer item, map item. Update the observation rule text in rules/handoff-layered-passes.md (~256-272), which says one classified object places one recipe at one column; no rules or docs file lists the kinds. designer_items must parse `rotation`; `_furniture_item` and the seen_furniture dedup must carry it; place_furniture must check every footprint column (per the #305 note). No world reading or redo: the re-read of 48,-44's tables and the decor redo are world work.
Check: python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_street_furniture, test_decor_layer and test_decor_plan pass. After a designer lists the 48,-44 tables, the decor plan contains a picnic_table row for each listed table (an unknown kind is dropped silently by decor_plan, so count plan rows, not refusals), each placed or carrying a named refusal reason (mind #303: dry runs on built cells understate until it lands).
On landing: the orchestrator logs the fix on I-008 (issues.py fix) with a check line for S-033; the implementer does not write to the world registry.
Follow-up not in this task: do decor furniture reads need more than z20 aerial? (owner suspicion; settle by comparing table sites at z20 and a finer zoom, and street view.)
